chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abdul Samad, from Al-Husayn ibn Hammad, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever says at the end of the obligatory prayer, before he puts on his legs (bends them to stand), 'I seek forgiveness of Allah, the One there is no god but Him, the Living, the Sustainer, of Majesty and Benevolence, and I repent to Him,' three times, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will forgive his sins, even if they were like the foam of the sea.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to recite after the obligatory prayer for forgiveness of sins?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith emphasizes the immediate transition from prayer to repentance, highlighting the Imam's instruction to recite the dhikr before fully rising from the prayer seat. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the boundless mercy of Allah, promising the forgiveness of sins 'like the foam of the sea' for this specific act of devotion. This practice serves as a spiritual bridge, ensuring the worshipper leaves the presence of the Divine with a cleansed heart.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa,, from Abdul Samad, from Al Husayn Bin Hammad, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The one who says at the end of the Obligatory Salāt, before he bends his legs, ‘Allahazwj is Who, there is no God except Himazwj. Heazwj is the Living, the Everlasting, with Majesty and the Benevolence, and I repent to Himazwj’, three times. Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic would Forgive his sins for him, and even if they were the likes of the foam of the sea (numerous)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ‘Abd al-Samad from al-Husayn ibn Hammad from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following: “

Whoever after an obligatory prayer and before moving his legs to a second position says, ‘I plead before Allah for forgiveness, no one deserves to be worshipped except Allah, the Living, the Guardian, the Possessor of Glory and Honor and to Him I return,’ three times Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, will forgive his sins even if they are as much as the bubbles of the ocean.’”
